question: Mechanical Properties of Fluids: Define pressure and write its SI unit.
gold_answer:
# Introduction

---

## Definition

Fluid pressure is defined as the normal compressive force exerted by a fluid per unit surface area of a container or object. 

Pressure acts perpendicular to the surface at every point, distributing uniformly across a level horizontal plane within a static fluid column.

---

## Characteristics

* **Isotropic Distribution:** At any given depth within a continuous static fluid body, pressure acts with equal intensity in all directions.
* **Scalar Nature:** Pressure is a scalar parameter because the force it produces acts in whatever direction face the surface points.

---

## Formula

The mechanical definition of surface pressure:

$$P = \frac{F}{A}$$

Where:
* $P$ represents the fluid pressure
* $F$ represents the normal force component acting perpendicular to the surface
* $A$ represents the total boundary area of the surface interface

---

## Metric System Units

The standard SI unit of pressure is the **Pascal ($\text{Pas}$)**, which is equivalent to a force of $1 \text{ Newton}$ acting uniformly over a surface area of $1 \text{ square meter}$.

$$1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N}/\text{m}^2 = 1 \text{ kg}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{s}^2)$$

---

## Summary

Pressure measures force distribution across a surface area, acting isotropically within fluid systems and measured internationally in Pascals.
